description: How is Postgres running? RED for txn_agg, then statements, connections and locks, rows and I/O, tables and vacuum, storage. From postgres_exporter: Postgres's own statistics, never table data.

panels.title: Transactions/s
panels.description: Rate. Committed plus rolled-back transactions per second in txn_agg, over the last minute.

panels.title: Rollback ratio
panels.description: Errors. Share of transactions rolled back over the last 5 minutes: a failed consumer batch (then retried one by one), a statement timeout, or an API error. 1% is a starting line, not an SLO.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Errors. Deadlocks Postgres detected in txn_agg over the selected range. Postgres cancels one side; any value is worth a look at the statements involved (Postgres logs them).

targets.expr: sum(((sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (datname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range]))))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Statement mean
panels.description: Duration. Statement time divided by calls over the last 5 minutes, every role. A route's latency is the sum of its statements plus pool wait. From pg_stat_statements (the 50 statements with the most time).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Client connections to txn_agg, any state. Orange above the budget of 32 (5 consumers × 3, API 10, Grafana 5, exporter 2); red near max_connections (100).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers over the last 5 minutes. Below 99% the working set no longer fits in memory and reads go to disk.

panels.title: Oldest open tx
panels.description: Age of the longest-running open transaction in txn_agg. A long one holds locks and stops autovacuum from cleaning dead rows. Orange from 1 minute, red from 5.

panels.title: Postgres up
panels.description: Whether the exporter could connect to Postgres on its last scrape. No data means the exporter itself is down, not necessarily Postgres.

panels.title: Rate: transactions/s
panels.description: Committed plus rolled-back transactions per second in txn_agg.

panels.title: Errors: rollbacks/s and deadlocks/s
panels.description: Transactions rolled back, and deadlocks detected, per second. A flat zero is healthy.

panels.title: Duration: mean statement time by role
panels.description: Statement time divided by calls per role. The consumers' batch insert writes up to 100 rows per statement, so it is slower per call than an API read.

panels.title: Max DB transactions/s
panels.description: The most database transactions committed or rolled back in one second, between consecutive scrapes. A consumer batch of up to 100 rows is one transaction, so this is far below the Consumers dashboard's transactions/s. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max DB transactions/min
panels.description: The most database transactions in any 60 seconds of the selected range. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max rows inserted/s
panels.description: The most rows Postgres inserted in one second. Rows skipped by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING are not inserts. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max busy connections
panels.description: The most connections executing statements at once, averaged over 10 s (statement time per second). Near the pool sizes (consumers 3 each, API 10) the pools, not Postgres, are the limit. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max connections
panels.description: The most client connections open to txn_agg. Orange above the budget of 32. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max statement mean
panels.description: The slowest minute of the range for the average statement. Rising with load means Postgres is the bottleneck; flat while throughput stops climbing means the limit is elsewhere. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: DB transactions/s (10 s resolution)
panels.description: Database transactions per second between consecutive scrapes.

panels.title: Rows inserted/s (10 s resolution)
panels.description: Rows Postgres inserted per second between consecutive scrapes. Should match the Consumers dashboard's rows inserted.

panels.title: Statements/s by role
panels.description: Statements executed per second, per login role.

panels.title: Busy connections by role
panels.description: Statement time per second: the average number of connections busy executing at once (Little's law, the same sizing as the pool budget). The dashed line is every statement in txn_agg, from pg_stat_database; the roles count the 50 statements with the most time.

panels.title: Slowest statements
panels.description: Statements in txn_agg that ran in the selected range, slowest mean first. Mean, total and rows count only the range. Share is this statement's part of all statement time in the range: the place to look when the database is busy. From pg_stat_statements: the 50 statements with the most total time, the exporter's own excluded. Click a statement to see its full text (cut at 200 characters).

panels.title: Connections by role
panels.description: Client connections to txn_agg per login role, stacked. Dashed line: the budget of 32. Each role carries its own CONNECTION LIMIT.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: Idle is normal: pools keep connections open. Idle in transaction means a client opened a transaction and stopped talking, holding its locks.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: Locks held or awaited in txn_agg. AccessShare is every read; a rise in RowExclusive is writes; anything Exclusive blocks readers.

panels.title: Oldest transaction by role
panels.description: Age of each role's longest-running open transaction. Red line at 5 minutes.

panels.title: Rows written/s
panels.description: Rows inserted, updated and deleted per second, as Postgres counts them. Inserts should track the Ingest dashboard's rows inserted/s.

panels.title: Rows read/s
panels.description: Returned: rows read by scans. Fetched: rows fetched through indexes. Returned far above fetched means sequential scans read rows they then throw away.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers. Dashed line at 99%.

panels.title: Temp files written/s
panels.description: Bytes queries spilled to temporary files because a sort or hash did not fit in work_mem. Zero is normal here.

panels.title: Sequential scans/s (top 10 tables)
panels.description: Full scans per second per table. On a small lookup table (categories) they are cheap and expected; on a transactions partition they mean a query missed its index.

panels.title: Dead rows (top 10 tables)
panels.description: Row versions left by updates and deletes, waiting for autovacuum. The transactions table is insert-only, so dead rows there come from rolled-back batches.

panels.title: Tables
panels.description: Every table in public, largest first; the transactions partitions are transactions_pYYYYMMDD. Scans count the selected range. Seq scans on a large partition from the API mean a query is not using an index. Dead % above 20% that does not come down means autovacuum is falling behind. An empty Since autovacuum means it has never needed to run.

targets.expr: sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) / ((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) + sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"})) > 0)

((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) - sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) - sum by (relname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}[$__range]))))

((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) - sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}) - sum by (relname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="public"}[$__range]))))

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: txn_agg on disk: tables, indexes and TOAST. pg_partman drops partitions older than 18 months, so it should level off.

panels.title: WAL size
panels.description: Write-ahead log segments on disk. Grows with write bursts and shrinks after checkpoints.

panels.title: Checkpoints/min
panels.description: Timed: on schedule (checkpoint_timeout). Requested: forced because WAL reached max_wal_size. Frequent requested checkpoints mean writes outpace the WAL size.

panels.title: Exporter scrape duration
panels.description: How long the exporter's queries take each scrape. It runs about a dozen catalog queries every 10 s as postgres_exporter (2 connections, 5 s timeout).
